definition_en: to run somewhere very quickly, or a small quick movement
core_image: 一个人低着头冲向雨中的公交站
scene: 雨忽然大了，他一路冲向街对面的屋檐。 He dashed across the road to the shelter.
sceneCN: 这里 dash 指「猛冲」（第 1 个义项：快速奔跑）；句意是他冲过马路跑到避雨处。

senses.title: Run with sudden speed
senses.definition: to move somewhere very quickly and without delay
senses.definitionCN: 飞快地、不耽搁地赶到某处
senses.example: He dashed across the road to the shelter.
senses.exampleCN: 他冲过马路跑到避雨处。
senses.why: A dash is short and urgent; it ends as soon as the goal is reached.
senses.whyCN: 猛冲又短又急，一到目的地就结束。

senses.title: A mark on the page
senses.definition: a short line used in writing to show a break or a jump
senses.definitionCN: 书写中用来表示停顿或跳跃的一道短线
senses.example: He put a dash between the two dates.
senses.exampleCN: 他在两个日期之间加了一道破折号。
senses.why: The pen moves fast, so the mark itself looks like a dash.
senses.whyCN: 笔走得快，画出的痕迹也像一次猛冲。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a small quantity thrown into something else
senses.definitionCN: 随手加进另一样东西里的一点点
senses.example: Add a dash of vinegar to the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 往汤里加一点醋。
senses.why: The amount is thrown in quickly, as a cook throws in salt.
senses.whyCN: 那点分量是随手甩进去的，就像厨师撒盐。

intro.en: Dash probably began as a word that imitated the sound and force of a blow.
intro.cn: dash 最初大概是一个模仿撞击声与力道的词。

items.en: The word echoed the noise of something struck hard.
items.cn: 这个词模仿硬物被击中的声响。

items.en: Dashen meant to strike or knock something violently.
items.cn: dashen 意为猛击或猛撞某物。

items.en: The sense of moving fast replaced the sense of striking.
items.cn: 「快速移动」的意思取代了「猛击」的意思。

items.en: The noun named the little line a quick pen leaves behind.
items.cn: 名词开始指快笔留下的一道短线。

items.en: A dash of salt meant the amount a cook throws in at once.
items.cn: a dash of salt 指厨师一次甩进去的那点分量。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one vowel, and the meaning group names faster and slower ways to move.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个元音，近义组则按快慢排列移动方式。

a long strip of cloth worn round the waist
a shallow container for food
to move with great speed and haste
to run at full speed for a short distance
to move suddenly like a thrown spear

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a foot pushing off wet ground and end with a pinch of salt falling into soup.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从湿地上蹬出的一只脚开始，落到落进汤里的一撮盐。

normal.en: A dash is a run that refuses to last.
normal.cn: 猛冲是一场不肯持续太久的奔跑。

normal.en: The mark on the page is the path of a pen in a hurry.
normal.cn: 纸上那道记号，是一支赶路的笔留下的轨迹。

normal.en: A dash of salt is speed measured in taste.
normal.cn: 一小撮盐，是用味道量出来的速度。

normal.en: When the rain starts, everyone discovers they can run.
normal.cn: 雨一下，人人都发现自己会跑。

normal.en: One word holds the runner, the mark, and the pinch.
normal.cn: 一个词同时装着奔跑的人、纸上的记号和一撮的分量。

abstract.en: Picture a figure bent forward against the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一个弓着身子顶雨前行的人影。

abstract.en: Picture a pen pulled across paper and leaving a straight scar.
abstract.cn: 想象一支笔划过纸面，留下一道直直的痕。

abstract.en: Picture a cook shaking salt once over a pot.
abstract.cn: 想象厨师在锅上抖一下盐。

examples.cn: 他冲过马路跑到避雨处。

examples.cn: 往汤里加一点醋。

examples.en: She dashed off a note before the meeting.
examples.cn: 开会前她匆匆写了一张便条。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dash 记成「哒嘘」：跑起来脚下「哒」一声，嘴里「嘘」一口气，一冲就到。

root: 中古英语 daschen 出现于十三世纪，最初模仿猛击的声响与力道，意为「猛撞」；十六世纪转为「快速移动」，十七世纪又指笔下划过的一道短线，十八世纪起再引申为「一小撮」的分量。

sensesIntro.en: From a body thrown forward, to a mark left by a quick pen, to a pinch thrown into a pot.
sensesIntro.cn: 从向前甩出去的身体，到快笔留下的一道痕，再到甩进锅里的一撮。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person running hard through sudden rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人顶着骤雨拼命奔跑。

branches.en: The first sense is the whole body moving at speed.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是整个身体高速移动。

branches.en: The second is the same speed reduced to a pen stroke.
branches.cn: 第二个把同样的速度缩小成一道笔画。

branches.en: The third is the same quick gesture applied to a powder.
branches.cn: 第三个把同样快速的手势用在粉末上。

branches.en: Both the runner and the pen cross a space without stopping.
branches.cn: 奔跑的人和笔都不停顿地穿过一段距离。

branches.en: A short line and a small amount are both things cut short.
branches.cn: 一道短线和一小撮，都是被截短的东西。

intro.en: Dash is a short family: a verb, an adjective of style, and compounds that grew from speed.
intro.cn: dash 这一族不长：一个动词、一个形容风度的形容词，还有几个从速度长出来的复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; dash is an English word of imitative origin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，dash 是英语中模仿声音造出来的词。

items.example: She dashed to catch the train.
He looked dashing in the old coat.
items.exampleCN: 他穿那件旧外套显得很潇洒。

items.example: The keys lay on the dashboard.
He made a dash for the door.
Use an em dash for the aside.

definition_zh: 吹嘘；自夸；拥有（值得自豪的事物）
definition_en: to talk too proudly about yourself
core_image: 拍着胸口夸耀的人
scene: 他拍着胸口，把成绩说了一遍又一遍。 He likes to boast about his new car.
sceneCN: 这里 boast 是「吹嘘」（第 1 个义项：过分夸耀自己）；句意是他喜欢炫耀自己的新车。

pos.zh: 动词：拥有，指值得自豪的事物

senses.title: To praise yourself too much
senses.definition: to talk with too much pride about what you have or have done
senses.definitionCN: 过分得意地谈论自己拥有的东西或做过的事
senses.example: He likes to boast about his new car.
senses.exampleCN: 他喜欢炫耀自己的新车。
senses.why: This is the central sense, loud self-praise.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义项，指大声地自我夸赞。

senses.title: To have something impressive
senses.definition: to possess something that is a source of pride
senses.definitionCN: 拥有某样足以自豪的东西
senses.example: The town boasts two fine museums.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇上有两座很好的博物馆。
senses.why: Places and things were said to boast of what they had.
senses.whyCN: 地方与事物也被说成在夸耀自己所拥有的东西。

intro.en: Boast began as a word for noisy display and settled on self-praise.
intro.cn: boast 本指喧闹的展示，后来固定在自夸这一意思上。

items.en: bost meant a noisy display.
items.cn: bost 意为喧闹的展示。

items.en: boast named loud self-praise.
items.cn: boast 指大声的自夸。

items.en: boast also meant to possess proudly.
items.cn: boast 也开始表示自豪地拥有。

items.en: boastful and boaster joined the family.
items.cn: boastful 与 boaster 加入这个词族。

items.en: boast covers bragging and proud possession.
items.cn: 如今 boast 兼指吹牛与自豪地拥有。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -oast ending; the near-meaning group names pride and bragging.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -oast 的词形；近义组是自豪与吹牛类词。

the land beside the sea

normalIntro.en: To boast is to turn your own praise up too loud.
normalIntro.cn: boast 就是把自己的夸奖声调调得太高。

normal.en: Boast about and boast of both take a thing.
normal.cn: boast about 与 boast of 后面都接对象。

normal.en: A hotel can boast a fine view.

normal.en: Boastful is the adjective.
normal.cn: 形容词是 boastful。

normal.en: A boaster talks about himself.

normal.en: Boast and roast differ by one letter.
normal.cn: boast 与 roast 只差一个字母。

abstract.en: See someone pointing at his own car.
abstract.cn: 想象有人指着自己的车。

abstract.en: See a chest puffed out in pride.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人自豪地挺起胸膛。

abstract.en: See a town sign listing its museums.
abstract.cn: 想象镇口的牌子列出博物馆。

examples.cn: 他喜欢炫耀自己的新车。

examples.en: Without boasting, I did most of the work.
examples.cn: 不是自夸，大部分活是我干的。

dict_mnemonic.text: boast 与 roast（烤）只差一个字母，自夸过头，就像被火烤着一样难受。

root: boast 源自盎格鲁诺曼语 bost（喧闹的展示），中古英语指大声自夸，十六世纪起又表示自豪地拥有某物，并衍生出 boastful 与 boaster。

sensesIntro.en: Loud praise of oneself, and the pride of owning something good.
sensesIntro.cn: 大声夸奖自己，以及拥有好东西时的自豪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man tapping his chest while talking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人边说边拍胸口。

intro.en: Boast adds -ful and -er to make an adjective and a person noun.
intro.cn: boast 加 -ful 与 -er 构成形容词和人物名词。

definition_en: a grey powder that hardens when mixed with water and is used in building, or to join things firmly together
core_image: 灰色粉末遇水变硬，把两块石头粘成一体
scene: 建筑工地上尘土飞扬。 Workers poured cement into the wooden frame.
sceneCN: 这里 cement 指「水泥」（第 1 个义项：遇水变硬的灰色建筑材料）；句意是工人把水泥倒进木模板里。

senses.title: A powder used in building
senses.definition: a grey powder made from lime and clay that hardens when mixed with water and sand
senses.definitionCN: 由石灰与黏土制成的灰色粉末，与水沙混合后变硬
senses.example: The wall is held together by cement.
senses.exampleCN: 这堵墙靠水泥黏合在一起。
senses.why: The Latin source meant rough broken stone, and the powder that binds such stones is the modern heir.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源义是粗糙的碎石，而把碎石黏住的粉末正是它的现代继承者。

senses.title: Something that binds people together
senses.definition: a shared feeling or interest that holds a group together
senses.definitionCN: 把一群人维系在一起的共同情感或利益
senses.example: Common work was the cement of the team.
senses.exampleCN: 共同的工作是这支队伍的黏合剂。
senses.why: If cement holds stones, any force that holds people together can borrow the same word.
senses.whyCN: 既然水泥能把石头黏住，任何把人维系在一起的力量都能借用这个词。

senses.title: To make something firm
senses.definition: to make a relationship, agreement or position stronger and harder to break
senses.definitionCN: 使关系、协议或地位更牢固、更难动摇
senses.example: The trip cemented their friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行巩固了他们的友谊。
senses.why: The verb applies the hardening of cement to any bond that becomes solid.
senses.whyCN: 动词把水泥变硬的过程用到任何变得牢固的纽带上。

intro.en: Cement goes back to a Latin word for rough cut stone, and only later named the powder that binds stones.
intro.cn: cement 可追到拉丁语中表示粗糙碎石块词，后来才指把石块黏住的粉末。

items.en: Caementum meant rough stone or rubble used in building.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caementum 指建筑用的粗石或碎石。

items.en: The noun comes from caedere, to cut, because the stone was cut into pieces.
items.cn: 该名词源自动词 caedere（切），因为石料是被切碎的。

items.en: Ciment named the binding material used with rubble in medieval walls.
items.cn: 古法语 ciment 指中世纪砌墙时与碎石同用的黏合材料。

items.en: English cement first means the mortar or binding powder itself.
items.cn: 英语 cement 最初就指灰浆或黏合粉本身。

items.en: Modern chemistry standardises the powder, and the verb extends to firm friendships and agreements.
items.cn: 现代化学使这种粉末标准化，动词义则扩展到牢固的友谊与协议。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the binding family, while the meaning group lists other building and joining materials.
note.cn: 形近组沿黏结词族展开，近义组列出其他建筑与黏合材料。

entries.definitionCN: 把颗粒黏结在一起的过程

entries.definitionCN: 由水泥、沙和砾石制成的坚硬建材

entries.definition: a soft mixture used to join bricks
entries.definitionCN: 用来砌砖的软质混合物

entries.definition: a substance that sticks things together
entries.definitionCN: 把东西粘在一起的物质

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the cut-stone root, the building compounds and the friendship phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用切石词根、建筑复合词以及友谊搭配。

normal.en: Cement comes from a Latin word for cut stone, because it began as rubble in a wall.
normal.cn: cement 来自拉丁语中表示切碎石料的词，因为它最初就是墙里的碎石。

normal.en: Cement, concrete and mortar are a stair: powder, then the mix, then the soft paste between bricks.
normal.cn: cement、concrete、mortar 像三级台阶：粉末、混合料、砖缝里的软浆。

normal.en: To cement a friendship is to let time harden the bond like setting cement.
normal.cn: cement a friendship 就是让时间像凝固的水泥一样把情谊变硬。

normal.en: Cement mixer keeps the word next to the machine that turns the powder into paste.
normal.cn: cement mixer 把词与那台把粉末变成浆的机器放在一起。

normal.en: The noun has no plural in ordinary use, so uncountable is the honest label.
normal.cn: 这个名词日常没有复数，所以标为不可数最诚实。

abstract.en: Picture grey powder sliding from a paper sack.
abstract.cn: 想象灰色粉末从纸袋里滑出来。

abstract.en: Picture a trowel smoothing wet grey paste over bricks.
abstract.cn: 想象泥刀把湿灰浆抹平在砖面上。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pressed together and held by something unseen.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手紧紧相握，被某种看不见的东西固定。

examples.en: The workers mixed cement and sand in a tub.
examples.cn: 工人把水泥和沙在盆里拌匀。

examples.en: A shared language cements the group.
examples.cn: 共同的语言把这个群体凝聚起来。

examples.en: The post is set in cement.
examples.cn: 这根柱子用水泥固定住了。

dict_mnemonic.text: cement 读音近似「塞门特」：把缝隙「塞」满，再「门」一关就黏牢了。

root: 源自拉丁语 caementum（粗石、碎石），出自 caedere（切），经古法语 ciment 进入英语，由石料转指黏合粉末。

sensesIntro.en: Cut stone becomes binding powder, the powder becomes a metaphor for human bonds, and the verb makes any bond harden.
sensesIntro.cn: 切碎的石料变成黏合粉末，粉末变成人际纽带的比喻，动词则让任何纽带变硬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: grey powder that hardens and locks two stones together.
core.cn: 核心意象：遇水变硬、把两块石头锁在一起的灰色粉末。

branches.en: The building powder keeps the physical sense closest to the Latin stone.
branches.cn: 建筑粉末义最接近拉丁语的石料本义。

branches.en: A shared interest binds people as cement binds stones.
branches.cn: 共同利益像水泥黏石头一样把人黏在一起。

branches.en: The verb hardens relationships the way cement hardens in air.
branches.cn: 动词让关系变硬，正如水泥在空气中凝固。

branches.en: Both depend on a material that sets and then cannot be moved.
branches.cn: 两者都依赖一种凝固后无法移动的材料。

branches.en: Both apply the builder's craft to human ties.
branches.cn: 两者都把建筑手艺用到人际纽带上。

intro.en: Cement forms abstract nouns with -ation and adjectives with -itious, plus the mixer compound.

latinIntro.en: Latin caementum and caedere are the stone and cut roots behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caementum 与 caedere 分别是这个词背后的石料与切割词根。

definition_en: to quote a source, to give something as an example or proof, or to order someone to appear in court
core_image: 论文脚注里列出的一个个人名与书名
scene: 论文写到最后，作者逐条核对来源。 She cited three studies in the first paragraph.
sceneCN: 这里 cited 是 cite 的过去式，指「引用」（第 1 个义项：提到他人的话或文字作为依据）；句意是她在第一段引用了三项研究。

senses.title: To quote a source
senses.definition: to mention words or writing from another source as support
senses.definitionCN: 提到他人的话语或文字作为依据
senses.example: She cited three studies in the first paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 她在第一段引用了三项研究。
senses.why: Latin citare meant to call, and calling a writer into your text became quoting.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 citare 意为召唤，把作者召进自己的文章便成了引用。

senses.title: To give as proof
senses.definition: to mention something as an example or as proof
senses.definitionCN: 举出某事物作为例子或证据
senses.example: He cited the falling sales as a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 他举出销量下滑作为警告。
senses.why: A summoned witness and a summoned fact both serve as proof.
senses.whyCN: 被召来的证人与被召来的事实，都是用来作证的。

senses.title: To summon to court
senses.definition: to order someone to appear in a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 命令某人出庭
senses.example: The driver was cited for speeding.
senses.exampleCN: 那名司机因超速被传唤。
senses.why: The oldest sense is legal: to call a person before a judge.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层意思属法律：把人叫到法官面前。

intro.en: Cite began as a Latin verb for summoning a person.
intro.cn: cite 最初是一个表示传唤人的拉丁语动词。

items.en: Ciere meant to set something in motion.
items.cn: ciere 意为使某物动起来。

items.en: Citare meant to call or to summon someone.
items.cn: citare 意为呼唤或传唤某人。

items.en: Citer narrowed to calling a person to court.
items.cn: citer 的词义收窄为传人出庭。

items.en: English cite kept the legal summons and added quoting.
items.cn: 英语 cite 保留法律传唤，又添上引用的意思。

items.en: Scholarship made citing sources an everyday act.
items.cn: 学术写作让引用出处成了日常动作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sound of cite, while the meaning group names quoting and summoning.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cite 的读音，近义组列出引用与传唤。

to order someone to appear

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the three same-sound words, the court origin and the academic habit.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用三个同音词、法庭来源以及学术习惯。

normal.en: Cite, site and sight sound alike, so check which one you wrote.
normal.cn: cite、site 与 sight 读音相同，写完要检查用的是哪一个。

normal.en: The oldest cite is a court summons, which is why a speeding driver is cited.
normal.cn: 最古老的 cite 是法庭传唤，所以超速司机会被 cite。

normal.en: To cite a study is to call the researchers into your own paragraph.
normal.cn: cite a study 就是把研究者召进你自己的段落。

normal.en: Citation is the noun, covering a footnote, a prize and a summons.
normal.cn: citation 是名词，涵盖脚注、表彰与传唤。

normal.en: Citing reasons is citing proof, not quoting words.
normal.cn: cite reasons 是举出证据，不是引用原话。

abstract.en: Picture a name in small print at the bottom of a page.
abstract.cn: 想象页面底部一行小字里的一个人名。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raising a folder to show one page in court.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭上一只手举起文件夹，翻出其中一页。

abstract.en: Picture a ribbon pinned on a coat for bravery.
abstract.cn: 想象外套上为表彰勇敢而别上的绶带。

examples.en: Please cite the original article, not the summary.
examples.cn: 请引用原始文章，而不是摘要。

examples.en: The report cites rising costs as the main cause.
examples.cn: 报告举出成本上升作为主要原因。

examples.en: Two officers were cited for their courage.
examples.cn: 两名警官因勇敢受到表彰。

dict_mnemonic.text: cite 与 site、sight 同音：写论文时要看清是引用、地点还是看见。

root: 源自拉丁语 citare（召唤），是 ciere（使动）的反复形式，本指传唤出庭，后转指引用。

sensesIntro.en: A court summons gives the idea of calling something in, which supplies both the quoted source and the proof.
sensesIntro.cn: 法庭传唤先给出「召来」的意思，由此生出被引的原文与被举的证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name listed in small print under a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：页面下方用小字列出的一个名字。

branches.en: Quoting is the everyday sense in study and writing.
branches.cn: 引用是学习与写作中最日常的义项。

branches.en: Citing proof calls a fact into the argument.
branches.cn: 举出证据就是把一项事实召进论证。

branches.en: The court summons is the oldest sense still in use.
branches.cn: 法庭传唤是仍在使用的最古老义项。

branches.en: A quoted source and a cited fact both support a claim.
branches.cn: 被引的原文与被举的事实都支撑一个主张。

branches.en: Citation can mean praise as well as a summons.
branches.cn: citation 既可指传唤，也可指表彰。

intro.en: The short stem builds a noun, two adjectives and the whole citation family.
intro.cn: 这个短词干构成名词、两个形容词以及整个 citation 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin citare and its base ciere supply the -ate pattern behind cite.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 citare 及其词基 ciere 提供了 cite 背后的 -ate 构词模式。

items.example: Cite the page number as well.
The judge cited the earlier ruling.
items.exampleCN: 法官援引了先前的裁决。

items.example: He was citing a long report.
items.exampleCN: 他正在引用一份长报告。
这篇论文有五十条引文。

latinEntries.example: Citare is the direct source of cite.
latinEntries.exampleCN: citare 是 cite 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Ciere is the older base of citare.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ciere 是 citare 更古老的词基。

definition_zh: 在艺术方面；有艺术性地
definition_en: in a way that relates to art, or with artistic skill
core_image: 从审美的角度去看待一件事
scene: 评审团围着一张照片讨论了很久。 The film is artistically ambitious but slow.
sceneCN: 这里 artistically 是「在艺术方面」（第 1 个义项：从艺术的角度衡量）；句意是这部影片在艺术上有野心，但节奏缓慢。

pos.zh: 副词：在艺术上；有艺术性地

senses.title: From an artistic point of view
senses.definition: judged by the standards of art rather than profit or speed
senses.definitionCN: 以艺术标准而非利润或速度来评判
senses.example: The film is artistically ambitious but slow.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在艺术上有野心，但节奏缓慢。
senses.why: The adverb marks the angle from which something is judged; adding -ly to artistic sets that angle as art.
senses.whyCN: 副词标出评判的角度；artistic 加 -ly 就把这一角度定为「艺术」。

senses.title: With artistic skill
senses.definition: done in a way that shows trained taste or craft
senses.definitionCN: 以显出训练有素的品味或手艺的方式完成
senses.example: The room was artistically lit for the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 房间为晚会打上了富有艺术感的光。
senses.why: The same adverb can describe the manner of the doing, not just the standpoint of the judge.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词也能描述做法本身的方式，而不只是评判者的立场。

intro.en: Artistically is artistic with the adverb ending -ally.
intro.cn: artistically 就是 artistic 加上副词后缀 -ally。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺」。

items.en: artist named a skilled maker.
items.cn: artist 指有技艺的制作者。

items.en: artistic described what belongs to art.
items.cn: artistic 描述属于艺术的事物。

items.en: The adverb appeared in art criticism.
items.cn: 这个副词出现在艺术批评文字中。

items.en: It now marks both judgment and manner.
items.cn: 如今它既标出评判角度，也标出做法方式。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same adjective; the near-meaning group gives other adverbs of aesthetic judgment.
note.cn: 形近组是同一形容词的变形；近义组是其他表示审美判断的副词。

entries.definition: of art
a maker of art
artistic skill
in terms of beauty
in an inventive way
with good judgment

normalIntro.en: Artistically tells you the yardstick is art.
normalIntro.cn: artistically 说明所用的尺子是艺术。

normal.en: It usually modifies adjectives such as gifted or ambitious.
normal.cn: 它常修饰 gifted、ambitious 这类形容词。

normal.en: The ending is -ally because the adjective ends in -ic.
normal.cn: 因形容词以 -ic 结尾，副词形式加 -ally。

normal.en: It can also describe how something is done.
normal.cn: 它也能描述某事如何完成。

normal.en: It contrasts with commercially or technically.
normal.cn: 它常与 commercially 或 technically 相对。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: ar-TIS-ti-cal-ly.
normal.cn: 重音在第二个音节：ar-TIS-ti-cal-ly。

abstract.en: See a judge holding a work at arm's length.
abstract.cn: 想象评判者把作品举远端详。

abstract.en: See a lamp angled to flatter a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象灯以妙角度照亮墙面。

abstract.en: See a hand choosing one colour out of many.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从众多颜色中挑出一种。

examples.en: The film is artistically ambitious but slow.
examples.cn: 这部影片在艺术上有野心，但节奏缓慢。

examples.en: The room was artistically lit for the evening.
examples.cn: 房间为晚会打上了富有艺术感的光。

examples.en: The two brothers are both artistically gifted.
examples.cn: 兄弟俩都有艺术天赋。

dict_mnemonic.text: artistic（艺术的）加 -ally：以艺术的方式或角度，就是「在艺术上」。

root: 由形容词 artistic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成；artistic 来自 artist，最终源自拉丁语 ars「技艺」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb marks the angle of judgment and the manner of making.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词既标评判的角度，也标制作的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a work held up and judged by one standard.
core.cn: 核心意象：作品被举起，以某一种标准衡量。

branches.en: artistically successful
branches.cn: 艺术上成功

branches.en: artistically ambitious
branches.cn: 艺术上有野心

branches.en: artistically arranged
branches.cn: 布置得富有艺术感

branches.en: artistically gifted
branches.cn: 有艺术天赋

branches.en: artistically valuable
branches.cn: 有艺术价值

intro.en: A regular adverb built on the adjective artistic.
intro.cn: 这是一个在形容词 artistic 上规则构成的副词。

latinIntro.en: The whole family returns to the Latin root ars, 'skill'.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都可回溯到拉丁语词根 ars「技艺」。

definition_en: shaped like a circle, moving in a circle, or a printed notice sent to many people
core_image: 一张印满字的纸被一份份传下去
scene: 办公室里每人手里都多了一张纸，内容一模一样。 The manager sent a circular to every department.
sceneCN: 这里 circular 指「通告」（第 3 个义项：印好并分发给多人的信函）；句意是经理给每个部门都发了一份通告。

senses.title: Shaped like a circle
senses.definition: having the shape of a circle
senses.definitionCN: 具有圆形的形状
senses.example: They sat at a circular table.
senses.exampleCN: 他们围坐在一张圆桌旁。
senses.why: Latin circularis described anything shaped like a small ring.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 circularis 描述任何像小圆环一样的东西。

senses.title: Moving around a circle
senses.definition: moving in a circle and returning to the starting point
senses.definitionCN: 沿圆周移动并回到起点
senses.example: The fan makes a slow circular motion.
senses.exampleCN: 风扇缓缓作圆周运动。
senses.why: A shape word also describes the motion that follows that shape.
senses.whyCN: 表示形状的词也用来描述沿这个形状进行的运动。

senses.title: A printed notice sent round
senses.definition: a printed letter or notice sent to many people
senses.definitionCN: 印好并寄发给许多人的信函或通知
senses.example: The manager sent a circular to every department.
senses.exampleCN: 经理给每个部门都发了一份通告。
senses.why: A letter sent round to many readers repeats the idea of going around.
senses.whyCN: 发给许多读者的信，重复的正是「绕一圈送达」的意思。

intro.en: Circular is the Latin adjective built on the word for a small ring.
intro.cn: circular 是拉丁语形容词，建立在小圆环这个词上。

items.en: Circulus meant a small ring.
items.cn: circulus 意为小圆环。

items.en: Circularis meant shaped like a ring.
items.cn: circularis 意为形状像圆环的。

items.en: English circular first described round shapes.
items.cn: 英语 circular 最初描述圆形。

items.en: The noun named a letter sent round to many readers.
items.cn: 名词义指发给许多读者的通函。

items.en: The adjective keeps the shape and the looping motion.
items.cn: 形容词保留了形状义与绕圈的运动义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin ring root, while the meaning group names round forms and notices.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语圆环词根，近义组列出圆形与通知。

entries.definition: a round closed shape
a closed path for electric current
a show performed in a ring
entries.definitionCN: 在圆环场地演出的表演

entries.definition: shaped like a circle or a ball
shaped like a ball
a printed announcement for many readers
entries.definitionCN: 供许多人阅读的印刷通知

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the -ar ending, the looping motion and the notice sense.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 -ar 词尾、绕圈运动以及通告义。

normal.en: Circular is simply circle plus an adjective ending, so it means circle-like.
normal.cn: circular 就是 circle 加形容词词尾，意为「像圆的」。

normal.en: A circular table has no head, which is why meetings like it.
normal.cn: 圆桌没有主位，所以开会时人们喜欢用它。

normal.en: A circular argument returns to where it started, like a ring of words.
normal.cn: 循环论证绕回起点，就像一圈词语。

normal.en: A circular letter is sent round to many readers, so the noun keeps the motion.
normal.cn: 通函被绕着发给许多读者，所以名词义保留了运动感。

normal.en: Circularity is the state, and circulate is the verb of the same family.
normal.cn: circularity 是状态，circulate 是同族的动词。

abstract.en: Picture a round table with every chair facing the same centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一张圆桌，每把椅子都朝向同一个中心。

abstract.en: Picture a fan blade tracing the same arc again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象扇叶一遍遍划过同一段弧线。

abstract.en: Picture the same printed sheet passing from desk to desk.
abstract.cn: 想象同一张印刷纸从一张桌子传到另一张桌子。

examples.en: The hall has a circular roof of glass.
examples.cn: 大厅有一个圆形的玻璃顶。

examples.en: The dancers moved in a slow circular pattern.
examples.cn: 舞者按缓慢的圆形队形移动。

examples.en: A circular was pinned to the notice board.
examples.cn: 公告板上钉着一份通告。

dict_mnemonic.text: circular 就是 circle 加 -ar：像圆一样。

root: 源自拉丁语 circularis（圆的），由 circulus（小圆环）加形容词后缀构成，兼指圆形的与传阅的通函。

sensesIntro.en: The ring shape gives the adjective, the ring motion follows it, and a letter sent round gives the noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 圆环形状先给出形容词，绕圈运动随之而来，绕着发送的信又给出名词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one printed sheet passed from hand to hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张印刷纸从一只手传到另一只手。

branches.en: The shape sense is the oldest adjective use.
branches.cn: 形状义是最早的形容词用法。

branches.en: The motion sense follows the outline of the shape.
branches.cn: 运动义沿着形状的轮廓展开。

branches.en: The noun names the paper that travels round.
branches.cn: 名词指绕行传阅的那张纸。

branches.en: Shape and motion are two views of one ring.
branches.cn: 形状与运动是同一个圆环的两种看法。

branches.en: Both senses keep something going around.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了「绕行」的意思。

intro.en: The stem circular builds a plural, two derived forms and a related verb family.
intro.cn: 词干 circular 构成复数、两个派生形式以及一组相关动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin circularis grows from circulus, the small ring behind circle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circularis 由 circulus 长出，后者正是 circle 背后的小圆环。

items.example: The office mailed two hundred circulars.
items.exampleCN: 办公室寄出了两百份通告。

items.example: The circularity of the design is striking.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计的圆润感很醒目。

items.example: The path runs circularly around the lake.
items.exampleCN: 小路绕着湖成环形延伸。

items.example: The circulation of air is poor here.

latinEntries.example: Circularis is the direct source of circular.
latinEntries.exampleCN: circularis 是 circular 的直接来源。

definition_zh: 有弹性的；可伸缩的；灵活的；橡皮筋
definition_en: able to stretch and return to its shape, able to change or be changed easily, or a rubber band
core_image: 一根橡皮筋被拉到两倍长，一松手又缩回原样
scene: 她把那根旧橡皮筋绕了两圈，纸卷始终没散。 A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
sceneCN: 这里 elastic 是「橡皮筋」（第 4 个义项：可拉伸回弹的环状橡胶制品）；句意是一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。

pos.zh: 形容词：有弹性的；可伸缩的；灵活的

forms.label: 比较级（形容词，多音节用 more）
最高级（形容词，多音节用 most）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「弹性；灵活性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「有弹性地」
由本词加否定前缀 in- 构成，义为「无弹性的；僵硬的」
由本词加 -ated 构成，义为「装有松紧带的」

senses.title: Able to stretch and spring back
senses.definition: able to be stretched and then return to its original shape
senses.definitionCN: 能够被拉伸，随后又恢复原来的形状
senses.example: The fabric is elastic enough to fit any wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 这块布料弹性足够，什么手腕都套得上。
senses.why: Elastic was coined from a Greek word for beaten metal that springs back, so the idea is a shape that returns.
senses.whyCN: elastic 由希腊语中表示「被敲打后能回弹的金属」的词造出，核心就是「会恢复的形状」。

senses.title: Able to change easily
senses.definition: able to change, adapt or be stretched in meaning without breaking
senses.definitionCN: 能够改变、适应，或在含义上被拉宽而不致崩坏
senses.example: The timetable is elastic enough to absorb delays.
senses.exampleCN: 这份时间表灵活得足以吸收延误。
senses.why: A material that springs back suggests a rule that gives and returns, so the adjective moves from rubber to arrangements.
senses.whyCN: 能回弹的材料让人想到一条会让步又收回的规则，于是这个形容词从橡皮走到了安排上。

senses.title: Responsive to price or demand
senses.definition: in economics, changing noticeably when price or income changes
senses.definitionCN: 在经济学中，随价格或收入变化而明显变化
senses.example: Demand for flights is highly elastic in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏季的机票需求弹性很大。
senses.why: A quantity that stretches with price behaves like rubber, so economists borrowed the same image.
senses.whyCN: 随价格伸缩的数量表现得像橡皮，于是经济学家借用了同一个意象。

senses.title: A rubber band
senses.definition: a loop of stretchy rubber used to hold things together
senses.definitionCN: 用来把东西捆在一起的环状弹性橡胶
senses.example: A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
senses.exampleCN: 一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。
senses.why: The adjective became a noun for the thing made of the material, the way a name for a quality becomes an object.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成了用这种材料做成之物的名词，就像一种性质的名称变成了实物。

intro.en: Elastic was coined in the seventeenth century from Greek elastos, beaten or ductile, and Latin elasticus, in the new science of materials.
intro.cn: elastic 是十七世纪在材料新科学中造出的词，源自希腊语 elastos（可敲打延展的）与拉丁语 elasticus。

items.en: The verb meant to drive or set in motion, and it lies behind the later adjective.
items.cn: 这个动词意为「驱动、推动」，是后来形容词的深层来源。

items.en: Elastos described metal that could be beaten out and would spring back.
items.cn: elastos 描述可被敲打成薄片又会回弹的金属。

items.en: Modern Latin formed elasticus as a technical adjective for materials.
items.cn: 近代拉丁语构成 elasticus，作为材料的专业形容词。

items.en: Seventeenth-century writers used elastic for gases and springs that recover their shape.
items.cn: 十七世纪的作者用 elastic 指能恢复形状的气体与弹簧。

items.en: The word spread to cloth, timetables, prices and finally to the rubber band itself.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到布料、时间表、价格，最后连橡皮筋本身也叫 elastic。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the elasticity family; the near-meaning group separates flexible, springy and plastic.
note.cn: 形近组收 elasticity 词族；近义组区分 flexible、springy 与 plastic。

entries.definition: The ability to stretch and return, or the responsiveness of demand.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「弹性；灵活性」，由 elastic 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: Not able to stretch, or not responsive to price.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无弹性的」，由 in- 加 elastic 构成。

entries.definition: Bands or strips of stretchy material, used in the plural.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数，指一根根弹性带。

entries.definition: Able to bend without breaking; it stresses bending rather than springing back.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可弯曲的」，强调弯而不断，而非回弹。

entries.definition: Bouncing back quickly, like a spring; more concrete and physical.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有弹力的」，像弹簧一样回跳，更具体。

entries.definition: Easily shaped when soft; it stresses moulding, not recovery.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可塑的」，强调塑形而不是恢复。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one rubber band, then let the same springiness travel into plans and prices.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子从一根橡皮筋出发，再让同样的回弹力走进计划与价格。

normal.en: Stretch it, let go, and it returns: that is elastic.
normal.cn: 拉长、松手、回到原样：这就是 elastic。

normal.en: An elastic timetable gives way and then closes again.
normal.cn: 有弹性的时间表会让步，然后又收回去。

normal.en: Economists call demand elastic when buyers stretch away from a price rise.
normal.cn: 价格上涨时买家就缩手，经济学家称这种需求为 elastic。

normal.en: The band itself takes the name: a bag of elastics.
normal.cn: 橡皮筋本身也用了这个名字：一袋 elastics。

normal.en: In- turns it stiff: inelastic.
normal.cn: 加 in- 就变硬：inelastic。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber band pulled to twice its length.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡皮筋被拉到两倍长。

abstract.en: The same give-and-return can describe a rule, a price or a schedule.
abstract.cn: 同一种「让开又回来」可以形容规则、价格或日程。

abstract.en: Elastic is any shape that remembers where it started.
abstract.cn: elastic 就是任何记得自己原位的形状。

examples.en: The fabric is elastic enough to fit any wrist.
examples.cn: 这块布料弹性足够，什么手腕都套得上。

examples.en: The timetable is elastic enough to absorb delays.
examples.cn: 这份时间表灵活得足以吸收延误。

examples.en: A thick elastic held the rolled papers together.
examples.cn: 一根粗橡皮筋把卷好的纸捆住了。

root: 源自希腊语 elastos「可敲打延展、会回弹的」，经近代拉丁语 elasticus 进入十七世纪科学英语，核心是「拉伸后恢复原形」。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses of elastic: springing back, bending to fit, responding to price, and the rubber band itself.
sensesIntro.cn: elastic 的四个义项：能回弹、能变通、随价格伸缩，以及橡皮筋本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rubber band stretched to twice its length and released.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根橡皮筋被拉到两倍长，然后松开。

branches.en: THE SPRING: the material returns to its old shape.
branches.cn: 回弹线：材料回到原来的形状。

branches.en: THE ROOM TO BEND: a plan or rule stretches and still holds.
branches.cn: 余量线：计划或规则被拉宽而依然成立。

branches.en: THE MARKET: buyers stretch away when prices rise.
branches.cn: 市场线：价格一涨，买家就缩手。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: the adjective becomes the name of the band.
branches.cn: 实物线：形容词变成了橡皮筋的名称。

branches.en: ONE IMAGE: physical springiness read into human arrangements.
branches.cn: 同一意象：把物理回弹读进人的安排里。

intro.en: Elastic is a scientific coinage from Greek and Latin; English adds -ity, -ally and the negative prefix in-.
intro.cn: elastic 是由希腊语与拉丁语造出的科学词汇；英语再加 -ity、-ally 与否定前缀 in-。

latinIntro.en: Greek elastos and Latin elasticus are recorded forms; the older Greek verb behind them is attested too.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 elastos 与拉丁语 elasticus 都是有记录的形式，其背后的更早希腊语动词也有书证。

definition_zh: 明显的；显而易见的；显著的；显眼的
definition_en: easy to see or notice, and large or important enough to attract attention
core_image: 白墙上一道新刷的痕迹，走过的人都忍不住多看两眼
scene: 换上新窗帘的那个下午，屋里一下子亮了许多，来串门的邻居刚进门就停住脚步。 The change in the room was noticeable the moment the door opened.
sceneCN: 这里 noticeable 是「看得出来的、明显的」（第 1 个义项：容易被人察觉）；句意为门一开，屋里的变化就一眼可见。图中可辨识物件：新窗帘、亮起来的窗、停在门口的邻居。

pos.zh: 明显的；显而易见的；显著的；显眼的

derivatives.zh: 由 noticeable 加后缀 -ly 构成，义为「明显地」
由否定前缀 un- 加 noticeable 构成，义为「察觉不到的」

senses.title: Easily seen or heard
senses.definition: possible to see, hear or feel without much effort
senses.definitionCN: 不用费多大劲就能看见、听见或感觉到
senses.example: There was a noticeable gap between the two shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 两层架子之间有一道明显的缝隙。
senses.why: The suffix -able marks what can be done to something, so noticeable literally means able to be noticed; the adjective begins with the eye's power to catch a thing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 标出「能被施加某动作」的性质，所以 noticeable 字面就是「能被注意到的」；这个形容词的起点，是眼睛捕捉东西的能力。

senses.title: Large enough to matter or to be measured
senses.definition: great enough in size or effect to deserve attention
senses.definitionCN: 在程度、数量或效果上大到值得关注
senses.example: The new drug produced a noticeable drop in blood pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 新药让血压出现了明显下降。
senses.why: Once a thing can be noticed, the word can also measure how much it deserves to be noticed, so the sense slides from visibility to degree and importance.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西既然能被注意到，这个词也就能衡量它值多少注意力，于是词义从「看得见」滑向「程度与分量」。

senses.title: Attracting attention by appearance
senses.definition: drawing people's eyes because of how a person or thing looks
senses.definitionCN: 因为外表而不断招来别人的目光
senses.example: In a crowd of grey coats her red scarf was noticeable.
senses.exampleCN: 在一群灰外套里，她的红围巾很显眼。
senses.why: A person or object that keeps pulling eyes is the same visible quality turned outward, which is how the adjective comes to mean standing out in a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 老是把人目光拉过去的人或物，是同一份「可见性」向外翻了出来，形容词因此多出「在人群中出挑」的意思。

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin-rooted English noun fitted with an English suffix; notice supplies the idea of being known and -able turns it into a quality.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是一个带拉丁词根的英语名词接上英语后缀：notice 提供「被知道」的观念，-able 把它变成一种性质。

items.en: The verb noscere, to get to know, gave notice its earliest idea of something becoming known.
items.cn: 动词 noscere 意为认识，给了 notice 最初的观念：某样东西被知道了。

items.en: Notitia, the state of being known, reached French as notice and then passed into English as a noun.
items.cn: notitia 表示「被知道的状态」，到法语写作 notice，再以名词进入英语。

items.en: By the sixteenth century English already had notice as a familiar noun for information and warning.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，英语里的 notice 已是表示消息与警告的常用名词。

items.en: The suffix -able, from Latin -abilis, was freely added to English verbs and nouns to mean able to be.
items.cn: 后缀 -able 源自拉丁语 -abilis，在英语中可自由加在动词和名词后，表示「能被……的」。

items.en: Noticeable settled in the eighteenth century and later gained the sense of a size or effect large enough to deserve attention.
items.cn: noticeable 在十八世纪定型，后来又添上「程度或效果大到值得注意」的含义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on notice; the near-meaning group collects adjectives for what is easy to see.
note.cn: 形近组收由 notice 构成的各种形态；近义组收表示「容易看见」的形容词。

entries.definition: In a way that is easy to see or notice.
entries.definitionCN: 以容易看见或察觉的方式。

entries.definition: So slight or well hidden that it cannot be noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 细微或隐蔽到无法被察觉的。

entries.definition: The noun and verb from which this adjective is built.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个形容词的名词与动词。

entries.definition: So clear that no explanation is needed.
Clearly shown by facts or signs.
entries.definitionCN: 由事实或迹象清楚显示的。

entries.definition: Very easy to see, often because of size or colour.
entries.definitionCN: 因大小或颜色而非常显眼的。

entries.definition: Just strong enough to be felt by the senses.
entries.definitionCN: 强度刚够被感官觉察的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a plain sum: notice plus -able, with the suffix doing nothing more than turning a pair of eyes into a quality of the thing seen.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是一次直白的相加：notice 加 -able，后缀只做一件事——把一双眼睛变成被看之物身上的性质。

normal.en: Noticeable is notice plus -able, meaning able to be noticed, and the final e of notice stays before the suffix.
normal.cn: noticeable 是 notice 加 -able，意为「能被注意到的」，notice 词尾的 e 在加后缀时保留。

normal.en: The same -able appears in readable, drinkable and washable, all meaning able to be read, drunk or washed.
normal.cn: 同一个 -able 也出现在 readable、drinkable、washable 里，都表示「能被读、喝、洗」。

normal.en: The negative is unnoticeable, with un- in front, meaning not able to be noticed at all.
normal.cn: 否定形式是 unnoticeable，前面加 un-，意为根本察觉不到。

normal.en: The adverb noticeably drops the final e and adds -ly, naming the manner in which something is seen.
normal.cn: 副词 noticeably 去掉词尾 e 再加 -ly，指某物被看见的方式。

normal.en: Noticeable difference is the everyday pairing, because the word measures how far two things stand apart.
normal.cn: noticeable difference 是最常见的搭配，因为这个词衡量的就是两样东西差得多远。

abstract.en: A change becomes noticeable at the moment someone else's eyes confirm what you already felt.
abstract.cn: 变化在别人的眼睛替你确认的那一刻，才算明显。

abstract.en: The suffix -able quietly turns a pair of eyes into a quality of the thing being looked at.
abstract.cn: 后缀 -able 悄悄把一双眼睛，变成了被看之物身上的一种性质。

abstract.en: What is noticeable is not only seen but weighed: the word asks how much attention a thing deserves.
abstract.cn: 明显的东西不只被看见，还被掂量：这个词在问一样东西值多少注意力。

examples.en: There was a noticeable gap between the two shelves.
examples.cn: 两层架子之间有一道明显的缝隙。

examples.en: The new paint made a noticeable difference to the hallway.
examples.cn: 新刷的漆让门厅明显不一样了。

examples.en: Her red scarf was noticeable in the grey crowd.
examples.cn: 在灰扑扑的人群里，她的红围巾很显眼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺替色波」——那块颜色扎眼得像块色布，走过的人都要看一眼；noticeable 就是明显的。

root: 由 notice（注意到）加形容词后缀 -able 构成；notice 一般认为来自拉丁语 notitia，源于 noscere（认识）。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective takes the noun's idea of being known and turns it into a quality: whatever can be caught by the eye, then whatever is large enough to matter, then whatever stands out in a crowd.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词把名词「被知道」的观念变成一种性质：先是能被眼睛捕捉，再是大到有分量，最后是在人群中出挑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fresh mark on a white wall that makes every passer-by look twice.
core.cn: 核心意象：白墙上的一道新痕，让每个路过的人都多看两眼。

branches.en: a gap between shelves the eye finds at once
branches.cn: 一眼就看见的架子缝隙

branches.en: a new curtain changing the light in a room
branches.cn: 新窗帘改变了屋里的光

branches.en: a test score rising by a clear margin
branches.cn: 考试成绩抬升了明显的一截

branches.en: a red scarf in a crowd of grey coats
branches.cn: 灰衣人群里的红围巾

branches.en: a change big enough to be talked about
branches.cn: 大到会被人议论的变化

intro.en: The adjective is a Latin-rooted noun joined to an English suffix, so its structure is as simple as it looks: notice plus -able.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是拉丁词根的名词接上一个英语后缀，结构看上去有多简单就有多简单：notice 加 -able。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 在……中间；在……之中；在……之间分配
definition_en: a variant of among used especially in British and literary writing, meaning surrounded by or included in a group
core_image: 旧书页上印着 amongst，纸边已经泛黄
scene: 老式信里，作者写道希望能在朋友中间度过晚年。 The writer hoped to grow old amongst friends.
sceneCN: 这里 amongst 是「在……中间」（第 1 个义项：处在某群体之内、被其围绕）；句意是作者希望能在朋友中间安度晚年。

derivatives.zh: 介词：在……之中，amongst 的标准形式
介词：在……之中，同样带 -st 的变体
连词：当……时，while 的 -st 变体
动词：混合；交往，与 amongst 同源

senses.title: In the middle of a group
senses.definition: surrounded by or in the company of a group, used especially in written or older style
senses.definitionCN: 被一群人围绕或与他们在一起，多用于书面或较旧的文体
senses.example: The writer hoped to grow old amongst friends.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家希望能在朋友中间安度晚年。
senses.why: The -st is an added ending that spread in Middle English, giving a longer, more formal-sounding form of among without changing the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -st 是中古英语扩散开来的附加结尾，使 among 多了一个更长、更正式的形态，词义并未改变。

senses.title: Shared within a group
senses.definition: used of something distributed or shared by the members of a group
senses.definitionCN: 指某物在一群成员之间被分配或共享
senses.example: The land was divided amongst the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 土地分给了村民们。
senses.why: Since amongst is only a longer among, it inherits the distribution sense as well, and the formal tone suits legal or historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 既然 amongst 只是更长的 among，它也继承了分配义，而正式语气正好适合法律或历史叙述。

intro.en: Amongst is among with an extra -st, a style choice rather than a different word.
intro.cn: amongst 是 among 加上 -st，只是文体选择，并非另一个词。

items.en: The phrase meant 'in the mingling, in the crowd'.
items.cn: 这一短语意为「在混杂中、在人群里」。

items.en: The fused form among became the everyday preposition.
items.cn: 合并形式 among 成为日常介词。

items.en: A final -st was added to some words, as in whilst and amidst, probably by analogy with superlatives.
items.cn: 一些词被加上词尾 -st，如 whilst 与 amidst，可能受到最高级形式的类推影响。

items.en: Amongst appears as a written variant and is favoured in older literature.
items.cn: amongst 在十三世纪作为书面变体出现，较受旧文学青睐。

items.en: British English keeps amongst in formal prose; American English prefers among.
items.cn: 英式英语在正式文章中保留 amongst，美式英语更常用 among。

note.en: The look-alike group shows the -st family; the near-meaning group gives the plain forms.
note.cn: 形近组展示 -st 词族；近义组给出普通形式。

sensesIntro.en: The longer form carries the same two uses as among: presence inside a group and sharing within it.
sensesIntro.cn: 较长的形式承接 among 的两类用法：处在群体之中，以及在群体内部分享。

scene: 她环游了世界。 She travelled around the globe.

senses.title: The earth

branches.cn: 手指在模型上找到一个国家。

branches.en: A glass ball glows above a lamp.
branches.cn: 一只玻璃球在灯上发光。

branches.en: The model is small, the earth is not.
branches.cn: 模型很小，地球并不小。

branches.en: A ball and a model share a round shape.
branches.cn: 球与模型共享圆形的轮廓。

intro.en: Globe is the base of global, globally, and globular.
intro.cn: globe 是 global、globally、globular 的词基。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is globus, a ball.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 globus，意为球。

items.example: The room was full of globes.
Climate change is a global problem.
items.exampleCN: 气候变化是一个全球性问题。

definition_en: the smallest unit of a chemical element, or a very small amount
core_image: 一颗小到不能再切开的小球
scene: 黑板上画着电子绕着中心转的圈。 The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
sceneCN: 这里 atom 是「原子」（第 1 个义项：构成元素的基本微粒）；句意是原子中心有一个原子核。

derivatives.zh: 动词：使雾化；使分裂成微粒

senses.title: Smallest unit of an element
senses.definition: the smallest unit of a chemical element that can take part in a reaction
senses.definitionCN: 能参与化学反应的最小元素单位
senses.example: The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 原子中心有一个原子核。
senses.why: Atom comes from Greek atomos, 'uncut', from a- 'not' plus temnein 'to cut', because the ancients thought it could not be divided further.
senses.whyCN: atom 来自希腊语 atomos「不可切分的」，由 a-「不」与 temnein「切」构成，因为古人以为它小到不能再分。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: a very small amount of something
senses.definitionCN: 极少的一点分量
senses.example: There is not an atom of truth in the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传言里没有一点真实成分。
senses.why: The smallest unit of matter became a measure of the smallest possible amount, used for emphasis in negatives.
senses.whyCN: 物质的最小单位被借来度量最小可能的分量，多用于否定句以加强语气。

intro.en: Atom is a Greek word that literally says 'not cuttable'.
intro.cn: atom 是个希腊词，字面意思就是「不可切分」。

items.en: temnein meant 'to cut'.
items.cn: temnein 意为「切」。

items.en: atomos meant 'indivisible'.
items.cn: atomos 意为「不可分割的」。

items.en: atomus named the smallest particle.
items.cn: atomus 指最小的微粒。

items.en: Atom entered scientific English as the basic particle.
items.cn: atom 作为基本微粒进入科学英语。

items.en: The word also became a figure for a tiny amount.
items.cn: 这个词也成了「极小分量」的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group is the atom family; the near-meaning group names particles and specks.
note.cn: 形近组是 atom 词族；近义组是表示微粒与少许的词。

entries.definition: relating to atoms
to break into fine particles
a device that sprays
a very small piece
a group of atoms
a tiny mark or bit

normalIntro.en: Atom means uncut: the piece nobody could divide any further.
normalIntro.cn: atom 意为不可切分，指那块谁也无法再分的微粒。

normal.en: The word is countable: an atom, two atoms.
normal.cn: 它可数：一个原子、两个原子。

normal.en: For emphasis in negatives, use not an atom of.
normal.cn: 否定句里用 not an atom of 加强语气。

normal.en: The adjective is atomic, not atomical.
normal.cn: 形容词是 atomic，不是 atomical。

normal.en: Do not confuse atom with molecule, which is a group.
normal.cn: 不要与 molecule 混淆，后者是原子的组合。

normal.en: Stress falls on the first syllable.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See a ball so small that no knife can enter it.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小到刀锋都进不去的球。

abstract.en: See a single dot of dust on glass.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃上的一粒尘点。

abstract.en: See a diagram of rings around one centre.
abstract.cn: 想象中心周围画着几个圈的示意图。

examples.en: The atom has a nucleus at its centre.
examples.cn: 原子中心有一个原子核。

examples.en: There is not an atom of truth in the rumour.
examples.cn: 这个传言里没有一点真实成分。

examples.en: A water molecule contains two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
examples.cn: 一个水分子含两个氢原子和一个氧原子。

dict_mnemonic.text: a-（不）加 tom（切）：不可再切的最小微粒，就是原子；再抽象一步，就是「一点点」。

root: 源自希腊语 atomos「不可分割的」，由 a-「不」与 temnein「切」构成，经拉丁语 atomus 进入英语；由最小微粒引申为极小的分量。

sensesIntro.en: The smallest piece of matter and the smallest possible amount share one limit.
sensesIntro.cn: 物质的最小一块与分量的最小一点，共用同一条底线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dot no knife can divide.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个刀也切不开的点。

branches.en: a carbon atom
branches.cn: 碳原子

branches.en: split the atom
branches.cn: 分裂原子

branches.en: a hydrogen atom
branches.cn: 氢原子

branches.en: not an atom of truth
branches.cn: 一点真实成分也没有

branches.en: not an atom of evidence
branches.cn: 一点证据也没有

intro.en: The Greek root tom, 'cut', links atom with anatomy and dichotomy.
intro.cn: 希腊词根 tom 意为「切」，把 atom 与 anatomy、dichotomy 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Greek atomos reached English through Latin atomus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 atomos 经拉丁语 atomus 进入英语。

definition_en: to look or seem like someone or something else
core_image: 两个人站在一起，侧脸轮廓几乎重叠
scene: 这对双胞胎长得太像，连老师都会认错。 The twins resemble each other so closely that even their teacher mixes them up.
sceneCN: 这里 resemble 是「像」（第 1 个义项：在外貌或性质上相似）；句意：这对双胞胎长得太像，连老师都会认错。

senses.title: To look like someone
senses.definition: to have a similar appearance to another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 外貌与另一个人或物相似
senses.example: She closely resembles her mother.
senses.exampleCN: 她长得很像她母亲。
senses.why: The Latin root means like, so the verb starts with visible likeness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「像」，所以这个动词从看得见的外貌相似开始。

senses.title: To have similar qualities
senses.definition: to share features or qualities with something else
senses.definitionCN: 与另一事物共享特征或性质
senses.example: Their styles resemble each other in many ways.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的风格在许多方面彼此相似。
senses.why: Likeness moves from faces to abstract patterns and styles.
senses.whyCN: 相似从面容扩展到抽象的模式与风格。

senses.title: To seem like something
senses.definition: to give the impression of being something, often in formal description
senses.definitionCN: 给人某种印象，常用于正式描写
senses.example: The room resembled a small museum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间看起来像一座小博物馆。
senses.why: The verb can describe an overall impression, not only a physical match.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可描述整体印象，而不只是外形吻合。

intro.en: Resemble comes from Old French resembler, from re- and sembler, to seem, ultimately from Latin similis, like.
intro.cn: resemble 来自古法语 resembler，由 re- 与 sembler（显得）构成，最终源于拉丁语 similis（像）。

items.en: Similis means like or similar.
items.cn: similis 意为相像、相似。

items.en: Similare means to make like.
items.cn: similare 意为使相像。

items.en: Sembler means to seem or appear.
items.cn: sembler 意为显得、看起来。

items.en: Resembler means to be like or resemble.
items.cn: resembler 意为相像、类似。

items.en: Middle English resemblen keeps the visual sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 resemblen 保留视觉上的相似。

items.en: Modern English extends resemble to styles, sounds, and situations.
items.cn: 现代英语把 resemble 扩展到风格、声音与情境。

note.en: Resemble is a likeness verb, and it sits near its family and near phrases for looking like.
note.cn: resemble 是一个「相似」动词，与自身词族以及表示「像」的短语相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being similar
similar to something
to bring people or parts together
to have a similar appearance
to look or behave like an older relative
to reflect or match something closely

normalIntro.en: Resemble contains the old root similis, like: to resemble is to be like.
normalIntro.cn: resemble 含有古老词根 similis（像）：相像就是「像」。

normal.en: The re- adds the sense of looking back and seeing the same shape.
normal.cn: re- 增添「回头一看还是同一个轮廓」的感觉。

normal.en: Resemble each other is the most common phrase.
normal.cn: resemble each other 是最常见的短语。

normal.en: Resemblance is the noun for the likeness.
normal.cn: resemblance 是表示「相似」的名词。

normal.en: We resemble family members in looks or manner.
normal.cn: 我们在外貌或举止上像家人。

normal.en: Compare look like: resemble is more formal and uses a single verb.
normal.cn: 对比 look like：resemble 更正式，而且只用一个动词。

abstract.en: Picture two shadows falling at the same angle.
abstract.cn: 想象两道影子以同样的角度落下。

abstract.en: Imagine a face in a photograph echoing another face.
abstract.cn: 想象照片中的一张脸与另一张脸遥相呼应。

abstract.en: Think of two melodies that share the same opening notes.
abstract.cn: 想象两段旋律以相同的开头几个音起句。

examples.en: She closely resembles her mother.
examples.cn: 她长得很像她母亲。

examples.en: Their styles resemble each other in many ways.
examples.cn: 他们的风格在许多方面彼此相似。

examples.en: The room resembled a small museum.
examples.cn: 这个房间看起来像一座小博物馆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + semble」——一再看到同样的样子，就是相像；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 similis（像）→ 俗拉丁语 similare（使相像）→ 古法语 sembler（显得）→ resembler（相像）→ 中古英语 resemblen → 现代英语 resemble。

sensesIntro.en: The verb begins with faces, extends to qualities and styles, and finally to the overall impression something gives.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从面容开始，扩展到性质与风格，最后指某物给人的整体印象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two outlines laid over each other until they nearly match.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个轮廓叠在一起，几乎重合。

branches.en: Physical likeness is the oldest and clearest sense.
branches.cn: 外貌相似，是最古老、最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Shared qualities extend likeness beyond appearance.
branches.cn: 共同性质把相似扩展到外貌之外。

branches.en: An overall impression can resemble something else.
branches.cn: 整体印象也可以像另一事物。

branches.en: People can look alike and behave alike at once.
branches.cn: 人可以同时长得像、举止也像。

branches.en: Shared qualities often create the impression of a match.
branches.cn: 共同性质常造成「相互吻合」的印象。

intro.en: Resemble is a French verb built on the Latin root for like, with English endings forming its family.
intro.cn: resemble 是建立在拉丁语「像」词根上的法语动词，词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin similis means like, and similare means to make like; French sembler means to seem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 similis 意为像，similare 意为使相像；法语 sembler 意为显得。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of repeated likeness.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「反复相似」的意思。

items.example: Similare turns the adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: similare 把形容词变成动词。

items.example: Sembler carries the root into French.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾

definition_zh: 极度的；最大的；最远的；极限
definition_en: of the greatest degree or amount, or the furthest possible point
core_image: 绳子绕到最后一圈，已经退到崖边再无可退
scene: 攀岩者背着伤员往下撤，绳子已经绷到最后一圈，面前只剩几步可走。 They treated the injured climber with the utmost care.
sceneCN: 这里 utmost 是「极度的、最大的」（第 1 个义项：程度达到极限）；句意为他们以最小心谨慎的方式照料那名受伤的攀岩者。绳子绕到最后一圈的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同源变体，义为「最远的；极度的」
同根副词，义为「完全地；彻底地」
同源比较级，义为「外面的」

senses.title: The greatest possible degree
senses.definition: used of a quality at the highest degree possible
senses.definitionCN: 形容某种性质达到可能达到的最高程度
senses.example: The matter is of the utmost importance to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事对这家人来说极其重要。
senses.why: The word began as the outermost point on a scale, so anything at that far end is at its greatest possible degree.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义是刻度上最外的一端点，因此处在那一点上的东西就达到了可能的最高程度。

senses.title: The furthest possible effort
senses.definition: used in the phrase do one's utmost, to try as hard as one can
senses.definitionCN: 用于 do one's utmost，表示尽最大所能
senses.example: She did her utmost to keep the meeting calm.
senses.exampleCN: 她竭尽全力让会议保持平静。
senses.why: If the outermost point is the limit, then to act to that point is to give everything one has.
senses.whyCN: 既然最外之点就是界限，那么把行动推到那一点，就是把所有力气都拿出来。

senses.title: The extreme limit as a noun
senses.definition: as a noun, the greatest extent of something such as power or effort
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指权力、努力等的最大范围
senses.example: The engines were pushed to the utmost.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机被开到了极限。
senses.why: The adjective's far end becomes a thing in itself, and people speak of the utmost as a boundary they reach.
senses.whyCN: 形容词所指的最外端点本身成了名词，人们便说「到了极限」这样一个被触及的边界。

senses.title: Carest and most attentive
senses.definition: used of attention or care that could not be exceeded
senses.definitionCN: 形容关照或小心已无以复加
senses.example: The old manuscripts were handled with the utmost care.
senses.exampleCN: 那些古旧手稿被极其小心地对待。
senses.why: Care also has degrees, and the outermost degree is the one that cannot be increased further.
senses.whyCN: 关照同样有程度之分，最外的那一档就是再无法增加的关照。

senses.title: Furthest away in place
senses.definition: describing the point furthest away or the end of an area
senses.definitionCN: 形容最远的点或一块区域的尽头
senses.example: They planted trees along the utmost edge of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在田地的尽头边缘种了树。
senses.why: The spatial sense is the oldest one, and the figurative senses of degree grew out of it.
senses.whyCN: 空间上的「最外」是最老的用法，程度上的引申义正是从这里长出来的。

intro.en: A double superlative in form: the old word out with the ending -most on top, meaning the outermost point.
intro.cn: 形式上是个双重最高级：古老的 out 加上最高级词尾 -most，意为「最外的那个点」。

items.en: Utmest and ytemest were formed from ut, out, with the superlative ending -mest.
items.cn: utmost 的古形 utmest、ytemest 由 ut（向外）加最高级词尾 -mest 构成。

items.en: The neighbouring Norse form útmastr with the same meaning reinforced the English word.
items.cn: 邻近的古诺尔斯语形式 útmastr 意义相同，强化了英语这一构词。

items.en: The word is used for the furthest edge of a place or a piece of land.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，这个词用来指某地或某块土地最远的边缘。

items.en: From the physical edge the word moves to the extreme of qualities such as care and importance.
items.cn: 从实体的边缘，这个词转向关照、重要性等性质的极限。

items.en: The phrase do one's utmost fixes the noun use in ordinary speech.
items.cn: do one's utmost 这个说法把名词用法固定在日常口语中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the old out family, and the near-meaning group gathers words for extremes.
note.cn: 形近组收集古老的 out 词族，近义组汇集表示极致的一类词。

entries.definition: the furthest or greatest possible
on the outside
furthest out
completely, with the same old stem, though the meaning has shifted
entries.definitionCN: 完全地；同出古词干，词义已偏移

entries.definition: at the very end of a scale
the largest possible
highest in rank or degree
very small in degree

normalIntro.en: See it as out plus -most: the most out you can go, and therefore the furthest degree.
normalIntro.cn: 把它看成 out 加 -most：能往外走到的最远处，也就是最大的程度。

normal.en: Utmost appears in fixed phrases such as the utmost care and the utmost respect.
normal.cn: utmost 常见于 the utmost care、the utmost respect 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Do one's utmost is the standard idiom for trying one's hardest.
normal.cn: do one's utmost 是「竭尽全力」的标准习语。

normal.en: Uttermost is an older variant with the same sense.
normal.cn: uttermost 是意义相同的旧变体。

normal.en: The word is nearly always used with the, not with a.
normal.cn: 这个词几乎总与 the 连用，而不与 a 连用。

normal.en: Utterly descends from the same old stem but now means completely.
normal.cn: utterly 同出这一古老词干，但今天意为「完全」。

abstract.en: Picture a rope paying out to its last coil at the cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象绳子放到崖边的最后一圈。

abstract.en: Hear the engineers push a machine to its loudest, hottest limit.
abstract.cn: 听工程师把机器推到最响最热的极限。

abstract.en: Give your last ounce of strength to hold a door shut.
abstract.cn: 用最后一点力气把门顶住。

examples.en: The documents were handled with the utmost care.
examples.cn: 这些文件被极其小心地处理。

examples.en: He did his utmost to explain the delay to the passengers.
examples.cn: 他竭尽全力向乘客解释延误的原因。

examples.en: Safety is of the utmost importance on the building site.
examples.cn: 在工地上安全是最重要的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「压到末寺」——被压到寺庙最后一角，已是退无可退的极限。

root: 古英语 ut（向外）加最高级词尾 -mest 构成 utmest，受古诺尔斯语 útmastr 影响定型为 utmost，本义「最外的点」

sensesIntro.en: One spatial edge gives the greatest degree, then the full effort, then the limit as a noun, then the care beyond which nothing can go.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个空间边缘先给出最大程度，再给出全力，再给出作为名词的极限，最后是再无法增加的关照。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope out to its last coil at the cliff edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳子放到崖边最后一圈。

branches.en: The degree branch: a quality at its highest.
branches.cn: 程度分支：某种性质的最高档。

branches.en: The effort branch: giving everything one has.
branches.cn: 努力分支：把所有的都给出去。

branches.en: The noun branch: the limit becomes a place to reach.
branches.cn: 名词分支：极限成了可以被触及的位置。

branches.en: The care branch: attention that cannot be increased.
branches.cn: 关照分支：再无法增加的用心。

branches.en: The space branch: the oldest, most literal edge.
branches.cn: 空间分支：最古老、最直白的边缘义。

intro.en: An old Germanic adverb of direction takes a superlative ending; there is no Latin element inside.
intro.cn: 一个古老的日耳曼方位副词加上最高级词尾，里面没有拉丁成分。

latinIntro.en: The word is wholly Germanic, so there is no Latin cognate family to list; the comparable Latin root would be extra, outside.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词完全属于日耳曼语系，没有可列的拉丁同族词；可作参照的拉丁词根是 extra（在外面）。

items.example: Ut- is the old form of out.
items.exampleCN: ut- 是 out 的古老形式。

items.example: The ending marks the extreme point.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记最远的端点。

items.example: Out is the modern form of the same word.
items.exampleCN: out 是同一个词的现代形式。

items.structure: related word with a different meaning
items.example: Utterly descends from the same stem.
Outer keeps the old stem in a plain adjective.
items.exampleCN: outer 把这一词干保存在普通形容词里。

items.example: The quality can be named abstractly if needed.
items.exampleCN: 必要时可以把这一性质抽象成名词。
inmost 走的是同一个 -most 模式。
topmost 再一次显示 -most 的构词力。

definition_en: an insect with large colourful wings that flies by day
core_image: 花丛间扇动彩色翅膀的小昆虫
scene: 花园里的花刚开。 A butterfly landed on the yellow flower.
sceneCN: 这里 butterfly 是「蝴蝶」（第 1 个义项：翅膀宽大的白天飞行的昆虫）；句意是一只蝴蝶落在黄花上。

derivatives.zh: 蝴蝶鱼，因外形和色彩像蝴蝶得名
蝴蝶效应，喻微小变化引起巨大后果
蛾，与蝴蝶同属鳞翅目，语义关联

senses.title: The colourful flying insect
senses.definition: an insect with two pairs of large colourful wings

senses.example: A butterfly landed on the yellow flower.

definition_zh: 领空；空域；可供飞行的开阔天空
definition_en: the sky above a country, regarded as its territory, or a defined area of sky used for a particular purpose
core_image: 国界线笔直向上延伸，裹住一柱有归属的天空
scene: 机场塔台里，值班员盯着雷达上不断移动的光点。 The pilot waited for clearance to enter the country's airspace.
sceneCN: 这里 airspace 是「领空」（第 1 个义项：一国管辖的上方空域）；句意为飞行员等待进入该国领空的许可。

pos.zh: 名词：领空；空域；可供飞行的天空

derivatives.zh: 复合词首成分，义为「空气、天空」，源自希腊语 aēr
复合词第二成分，义为「空间」，源自拉丁语 spatium
与 airspace 共用 air 与 space 两个成分，义为「航空航天」

senses.title: The sky above a nation
senses.definition: the column of sky above a country, treated in law as part of its territory
senses.definitionCN: 一国领土上方的空域，在法律上被视为该国领土的一部分
senses.example: The aircraft was ordered to leave national airspace immediately.
senses.exampleCN: 这架飞机被要求立即离开该国领空。
senses.why: Air plus space turns the sky into a place: a border drawn on land can be extended straight upward, and the column it encloses belongs to someone.
senses.whyCN: air 与 space 合起来把天空变成一个地方：地上的国界可以笔直向上延伸，围出的这一柱空气就有了归属。

senses.title: A controlled zone of sky
senses.definition: a defined block of sky that an authority sets aside for a purpose or controls for safety
senses.definitionCN: 由主管机构划定用途或为安全而加以管制的特定天空区块
senses.example: Controllers divided the airspace into arrival and departure corridors.
senses.exampleCN: 管制员把这片空域划分为进港和离港走廊。
senses.why: Once the sky is a place, it can be surveyed and cut into blocks, just as land is cut into districts with rules for each.
senses.whyCN: 天空一旦成为地方，就能像土地划区那样被测量、切块，并为每一块定下规则。

senses.title: Open sky available for flight
senses.definition: the open sky left free for aircraft, kites, or other flying objects
senses.definitionCN: 留供飞机、风筝或其他飞行物使用的开阔天空
senses.example: The kite climbed until it reached open airspace above the trees.
senses.exampleCN: 风筝一直上升，直到进入树梢之上的开阔空域。
senses.why: This is the compound at its plainest: air as empty room and space as room to move, with no border or controller in sight.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个复合词最朴素的用法：air 是空气，space 是可活动的余地，既没有边界也没有管制员。

intro.en: Airspace joins a Greek word for the misty lower air to a Latin word for extent, and aviation gave the pair a legal meaning.
intro.cn: airspace 把希腊语中表示低处雾气般空气的词，接到拉丁语表示范围、空间的词上，航空业又给这对组合添了法律含义。

items.en: Greek aēr named the lower, misty air that people breathe, as opposed to the bright upper sky.
items.cn: 希腊语 aēr 指人呼吸的、低处带雾的空气，与明亮的上层天空相对。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as aer, still meaning air, and passed it to French and English.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入希腊词作 aer，仍指空气，再经法语传入英语。

items.en: Old French air carried the word into English, where air soon also meant the open sky.
items.cn: 古法语 air 把这个词带入英语，air 很快也指开阔的天空。

items.en: Latin spatium meant an extent or interval, the source of English space and of spacious.
items.cn: 拉丁语 spatium 意为范围、间隔，是英语 space 与 spacious 的来源。

items.en: Aviation needed one word for the sky as property and as a managed zone, so air and space were joined.
items.cn: 航空业需要用一个词同时表达「作为财产的天空」和「被管理的天空」，于是把 air 与 space 合在一起。

items.en: Treaties fixed the principle that each state controls the airspace above its land and waters.
items.cn: 各项条约确立了每个国家管辖其陆地与水域上方领空的原则。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from the same two halves; the near-meaning group gathers words for sky, territory and zones.
note.cn: 形近组收由同样两个成分构成的词；近义组收表示天空、领土与区域的词。

entries.definition: The noun for the mixture of gases around the earth, also used for the open sky.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指地球周围的气体混合物，也用来指开阔的天空。

entries.definition: The noun for room or extent, the second half of airspace.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指空间或范围，是 airspace 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The industry and technology of aircraft and spacecraft together.
entries.definitionCN: 指航空与航天合在一起的产业与技术。

entries.definition: The visible space above the earth, without any legal or managed sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指地面上方可见的空间，不带法律或管制含义。

entries.definition: An area under a state's control, usually land, but law can extend it upward.
entries.definitionCN: 指一国控制的区域，通常是陆地，法律也可将其向上延伸。

entries.definition: An area marked off for a particular purpose, the model behind a controlled airspace block.
entries.definitionCN: 指为特定用途划出的区域，是管制空域区块的模型。

normalIntro.en: These hooks split the compound into air and space and attach each half to something you can see.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把复合词拆成 air 与 space，并让每一半都挂上看得见的东西。

normal.en: Airspace is air plus space: the sky treated as real estate.
normal.cn: airspace 是 air 加 space：把天空当成地产。

normal.en: A border on the ground can be drawn upward, and the column above it is national airspace.
normal.cn: 地上的国界可以向上画，它上方的那一柱就是领空。

normal.en: Controlled airspace is sky with lanes and rules, like a highway in the air.
normal.cn: controlled airspace 是有航线和规则的天空，像空中的高速公路。

normal.en: A drone that crosses a line without permission violates airspace.
normal.cn: 无人机未经许可越过界线，就是侵犯领空。

normal.en: Open airspace is simply room to fly, with no owner and no controller.
normal.cn: open airspace 只是可供飞行的余地，没有归属也没有管制。

abstract.en: Picture a fence standing on a hill, then pull the fence straight up into the clouds.
abstract.cn: 想象山顶上立着一道篱笆，再把这道篱笆笔直拉进云里。

abstract.en: The fence leaves a shadow-column of sky behind it, and that column has a name.
abstract.cn: 篱笆在身后留下一柱带影子的天空，这一柱天空有了名字。

abstract.en: Turn the column sideways and it becomes a corridor through which planes slide.
abstract.cn: 把这一柱天空横过来，它就成了飞机穿行的走廊。

examples.en: The drone flew into restricted airspace near the border.
examples.cn: 无人机飞入了边境附近的限制空域。

examples.en: The tower closed the airspace because of heavy fog.
examples.cn: 塔台因大雾关闭了该空域。

examples.en: Every country claims the airspace above its territory.
examples.cn: 每个国家都主张其领土上方的领空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「空气 空间」——空气加空间，就是划出来的一片天

root: 英语复合词：air（空气、天空，源自希腊语 aēr，经拉丁语 aer 与古法语 air 入英语）+ space（空间，源自拉丁语 spatium），字面为「天空中的一片空间」。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses treat the sky as national territory, as a managed zone, and as open room for flight.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项分别把天空看作国家领土、被管理的区域，以及可供飞行的开阔空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a border line on the ground is extended straight upward, and the column of sky above it becomes a place with an owner.
core.cn: 核心意象：地上的国界线笔直向上延伸，它上方那一柱天空就成了有归属的地方。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the line on the ground rises into the sky and marks an owned column of air.
branches.cn: 边界线：地上的线升到空中，标出一柱有归属的空气。

branches.en: THE STATE: international law accepts that a country's territory includes the sky above it.
branches.cn: 国家线：国际法承认一国领土包括其上方天空。

branches.en: THE MANAGER: aviation authorities cut the sky into blocks with rules and corridors.
branches.cn: 管理线：航空当局用规则和走廊把天空切成块。

branches.en: THE OPEN SKY: beyond the controlled blocks there is still room for a kite or a glider.
branches.cn: 开阔线：在管制区块之外，仍有供风筝或滑翔机使用的空间。

branches.en: THE CROSSING: a flight moves from one controlled block into open sky and back again.
branches.cn: 穿越线：一次飞行从某个管制区块进入开阔天空，再返回。

intro.en: Airspace is a transparent English compound whose interest lies in joining a natural element to a legal idea of space.
intro.cn: airspace 是一个透明的英语复合词，其趣味在于把自然元素接到法律意义上的空间概念上。

latinIntro.en: Both halves reach back through Latin to Greek or to an older Latin stem, and the deeper origin of each is only partly certain.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都经由拉丁语上溯到希腊语或更早的拉丁词干，各自更深的来源只部分确定。

items.meaning: the mixture of gases we breathe

items.example: The box takes up little space.
items.exampleCN: 这个盒子占的空间很小。

管制员重新划分了这个空域块。

items.exampleCN: 每个空域使用者都必须提交飞行计划。

definition_en: sensible and likely to bring a good result, and therefore worth doing or choosing
core_image: 山路入口竖着一块牌子，提示前方塌方、请走另一侧
scene: 天色转暗，向导抬头看了看压下来的云层。 It is advisable to begin the descent before the storm arrives.
sceneCN: 这里的 advisable 是「明智的、可取的」（第 1 个义项：值得采取、能避免麻烦的）；句意是在暴风雨到来之前开始下撤是明智的。

pos.zh: 形容词：明智的；可取的；适宜的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -able 还原为动词，义为「建议；劝告」
同源名词，义为「建议；忠告」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「顾问」
加 -ory 构成，义为「咨询的；劝告性的」

senses.title: Wise and worth doing
senses.definition: sensible because it is likely to produce a good result or avoid trouble
senses.definitionCN: 因为很可能带来好结果或避开麻烦而显得明智的
senses.example: It is advisable to begin the descent before the storm arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 在暴风雨到来之前开始下撤是明智的。
senses.why: The suffix -able makes the word mean 'able to be advised': an action that a sensible adviser would recommend is advisable.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 让这个词表示「值得被建议的」：一个明智的顾问会推荐的做法，就是 advisable。

senses.title: Suitable as a measure
senses.definition: described of a plan or measure that is judged proper and suitable in a formal context
senses.definitionCN: 正式语境中形容某项方案或措施被认为恰当、适宜
senses.example: The committee treated a full review as the advisable course.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会认为全面复查才是可取的做法。
senses.why: Placed before a noun, the word shifts from 'it would be wise to' to 'judged proper as a measure', which is how official reports use it.
senses.whyCN: 放在名词前时，它从「这样做会明智」转为「作为措施被认为得当」，官方报告正是这样用的。

intro.en: An adjective formed in English from advise, which itself came from Latin through French.
intro.cn: 这是英语在动词 advise 上构成的形容词，而 advise 本身经由法语来自拉丁语。

items.en: videre, to see, gave visum, 'what seems', the base of the whole advice family.
items.cn: videre 意为「看」，其分词 visum 表示「看来如此之物」，是整族词的底子。

items.en: Medieval Latin advisare meant to consider or take counsel, built on the same 'seem' root.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 advisare 意为「考虑、商议」，同样建立在「看来如此」这个词根上。

items.en: Old French aviser meant to look at, consider, or give an opinion, and English borrowed it as advise.
items.cn: 古法语 aviser 意为「察看、考虑、给出意见」，英语借入后成为 advise。

items.en: English added -able to advise, first in the sense 'able to be advised', then 'worth advising'.
items.cn: 英语给 advise 加上 -able，先表示「可以被告知的」，后来转为「值得建议的」。

items.en: Today the word almost always appears in the frame it is advisable to do something, especially in guidance and rules.
items.cn: 今天它几乎总出现在「it is advisable to do something」这一句框里，多见于指南与规章。

note.en: The first group shares the advice root; the second gathers adjectives of prudence and suitability.
note.cn: 第一组共享 advice 词根；第二组收表示「审慎、适宜」的形容词。

entries.definition: to give advice or inform someone
an opinion offered to guide action
giving advice rather than making rules
in a way that is sensible; a rare adverb
entries.definitionCN: 明智地；罕见的副词形式

entries.definition: showing good judgment; broader than advisable
entries.definitionCN: 明智的；比 advisable 更宽泛

entries.definition: careful about the future and avoiding risk
entries.definitionCN: 审慎的；注重规避风险的

entries.definition: put forward as the thing to choose
fitting the situation; says nothing about wisdom
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；不涉及是否明智

normalIntro.en: The word is advise plus -able, so it names an action that deserves to be advised.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 advise 加 -able，指一种值得被建议采取的做法。

normal.en: advise plus -able gives 'worth advising', hence wise to do.
normal.cn: advise 加 -able 就是「值得被建议的」，因此是「明智的」。

normal.en: The usual frame is it is advisable to do something.
normal.cn: 最常见的句框是「it is advisable to do something」。

normal.en: Unlike advice, the adjective has no -ice spelling trap.
normal.cn: 与名词 advice 不同，这个形容词没有 -ice 的拼写陷阱。

normal.en: Highly advisable is the common intensifier in official guidance.
normal.cn: highly advisable 是官方指南里常见的加强说法。

normal.en: The root visum, what seems, also lies behind vision and evident.
normal.cn: 词根 visum（看来如此）也藏在 vision 与 evident 背后。

abstract.en: Picture a warning board at a trailhead pointing to the safer path.
abstract.cn: 想象登山口一块警示牌，指向更安全的那条路。

abstract.en: See a committee underlining one line of a report as the course to take.
abstract.cn: 想象委员会在报告里给一行字划线，标出该走的路线。

abstract.en: Imagine advice turned into an adjective, so the opinion becomes a property of the act.
abstract.cn: 想象建议变成一个形容词，意见于是成了那个动作本身的属性。

examples.en: It is advisable to book tickets well before the holiday.
examples.cn: 最好在假期前尽早订票。

examples.en: Regular checks are advisable for any old electrical wiring.
examples.cn: 任何老旧的电路都宜定期检查。

examples.en: The doctor thought a second opinion advisable.
examples.cn: 医生认为再听取一位医生的意见是明智的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱德外则伯」——爱得我特地在外面问了一圈，才说这做法可取。

root: 由动词 advise 加后缀 -able 构成；advise 经古法语 aviser 上溯中世纪拉丁语 advisare，再往前是拉丁语 videre「看」与 visum「看来如此」。

sensesIntro.en: One judgment of good sense appears twice: as a general verdict on an action, and as a formal label on a chosen measure.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「有道理」的判断出现两次：一次是对某动作的总体评断，一次是给某项措施贴上的正式标签。

branches.en: a full review adopted as the proper measure

branches.en: an official report naming the course to take

latinIntro.en: visum and advisare are recorded forms; the -able adjective is a later English build.

definition_zh: 必不可少的；不可或缺的
definition_en: so important that it cannot be done without
core_image: 一栋房子没了承重的那根柱，整片屋顶都会塌下来
scene: 收拾行李时，总有几样东西放不下也带不走。 A good dictionary is indispensable for a translator.
sceneCN: 这里 indispensable 是「不可或缺的」（第 1 个义项：少了就不行）；句意是译者的好词典是少不了的。

pos.zh: 形容词：必不可少的；不可或缺的

collocations.phrase: an indispensable member of the team
collocations.zh: 团队中不可缺少的一员

derivatives.zh: 义为「可省去的」，去掉 in- 即成反义
义为「分发、配药」，是本词的动词根

senses.title: Cannot be done without
senses.titleCN: 不可少：少了就无法完成
senses.definition: too necessary to be given up or left out
senses.definitionCN: 太必要，以致不能舍弃或省略
senses.example: A good dictionary is indispensable for a translator.
senses.exampleCN: 对译者来说，一部好词典是少不了的。
senses.why: Latin dispensare means to weigh out and distribute, and in- with -able says this cannot be excused from the count.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dispensare 意为「称量分发」，in- 加 -able 表示这种东西不能从账上免掉。

senses.title: Of a person, no substitute available
senses.titleCN: 无可替代：指某人无可取代
senses.definition: describing a person whose role nobody else can fill
senses.definitionCN: 形容某人的角色无人能替
senses.example: She is indispensable to the small clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 对这家小诊所来说，她是不可或缺的。
senses.why: A role, like a supply, can run out: without this person the work stops.
senses.whyCN: 角色也像物资，会断供：没有这个人，工作就停。

senses.title: Of an object, part of routine life
senses.titleCN: 日用必需：已成生活惯例
senses.definition: of a thing, so woven into daily habit that its absence is felt at once
senses.definitionCN: 指某物已融入日常习惯，一缺立刻被察觉
senses.example: The phone has become indispensable in daily life.
senses.exampleCN: 手机在日常生活中已变得不可或缺。
senses.why: Habit makes things necessary even when nothing forces us to keep them.
senses.whyCN: 习惯让东西变得必要，哪怕没有外力逼我们留着。

senses.title: In philosophy, absolutely necessary
senses.titleCN: 哲理用法：绝对必需之物
senses.definition: in abstract argument, something whose absence would make the whole system fail
senses.definitionCN: 在抽象论证中，指缺失会使整个体系崩塌的东西
senses.example: Trust is indispensable to any lasting agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 对任何持久的约定来说，信任都是不可或缺的。
senses.why: The word rises from goods to ideas: what cannot be dispensed with in logic is just as concrete.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从货物升到观念：逻辑上省不掉的东西，同样具体。

intro.en: Indispensable is in-, not, plus dispensable, from Latin dispensare, to weigh out and share.
intro.cn: indispensable 是 in-（不）加 dispensable，后者源自拉丁语 dispensare「称量分发」。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang, and so to weigh.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂」，进而指「称重」。

items.en: Dispensare meant to weigh out and hand out shares.
items.cn: dispensare 意为称量后分发各份。

items.en: Dispensare also meant to grant exemption from a rule.
items.cn: dispensare 又指免除某项规矩。

items.en: Indispensable appeared for duties that could not be excused.
items.cn: indispensable 起初用于不能免除的义务。

items.en: The word widened to mean anything no plan can go without.
items.cn: 后来词义扩大，指任何计划都省不掉的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -pens- weighing root; the near-meaning group holds words for necessity.
note.cn: 形近组共用 -pens-「称量」词根；近义组收表示必要性的词。

entries.definition: That can be done without.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可省去的」，与本词相反。

entries.definition: To give out or to do without.
Money paid out.
Absolutely necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「必需的」，语气最重。

entries.definition: Necessary for life or success.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「至关重要的」。

entries.definition: Decisive for the outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「关键的」，重在决定结果。

normalIntro.en: The hooks use the load-bearing column and the account from which nothing can be excused.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子借房子的承重柱，以及一笔什么也免不掉的账。

normal.en: In plus dispensable: cannot be dispensed with, cannot be struck off the list.
normal.cn: in 加 dispensable：省不掉，也划不掉。

normal.en: Imagine a table missing one leg: the missing leg was indispensable.
normal.cn: 想一张少了一条腿的桌子：缺的那条正是不可缺的。

normal.en: The -able says it can be dispensed with; the in- says no, not this one.
normal.cn: -able 说「可以省」，in- 说：这一个不行。

normal.en: A pharmacist dispenses medicine; what cannot be dispensed is indispensable.
normal.cn: 药剂师 dispense 药；不能 dispense 掉的，就是 indispensable。

normal.en: Used of people, the word is a compliment, but also a warning about workload.
normal.cn: 用在人身上，这是夸奖，也是关于工作量的警告。

abstract.en: What is indispensable is defined by a counterfactual: the plan fails without it.
abstract.cn: 「不可或缺」由反事实定义：没有它，计划就失败。

abstract.en: Necessity is often manufactured by habit rather than by nature.
abstract.cn: 必要性常由习惯制造，而非由天性规定。

abstract.en: Every system hides one part it could never replace, and that part holds it up.
abstract.cn: 每个系统都藏着一个再也换不掉的部件，而正是它把系统撑住。

examples.en: Clean water is indispensable to public health.
examples.cn: 清洁的水对公共卫生不可或缺。

examples.en: He soon made himself indispensable at the office.
examples.cn: 他很快成了办公室里离不开的人。

examples.en: Bicycles are indispensable in this flat town.
examples.cn: 在这座平坦的小城里，自行车必不可少。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬地斯彭瑟伯」——硬地上的那台喷雾器是干活必不可少的。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ dispensare（称量分发、免除），源出 pendere（悬挂、称重）；同根词 dispense、dispensable、expense、pendant。

sensesIntro.en: Indispensable says that one item cannot be taken off the list: it holds for tools, for people, for habits and for ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: indispensable 说的是某样东西不能从清单上划掉：工具如此，人、习惯与观念也如此。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load-bearing column without which the roof falls.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根抽掉屋顶就塌的承重柱。

branches.en: TOOL LINE: an object the work cannot start without.
branches.cn: 工具线：没它工作就开不了。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: a role nobody else can fill.
branches.cn: 人物线：一个没人能补上的角色。

branches.en: HABIT LINE: a thing whose absence is felt at once.
branches.cn: 习惯线：一缺就立刻被察觉的东西。

branches.en: THEORY LINE: a condition the whole system rests on.
branches.cn: 理论线：整个体系所依赖的条件。

branches.en: VALUE LINE: praise for a person, warning for a team.
branches.cn: 价值线：对人人是赞美，对团队是警示。

intro.en: A negative prefix stacked on a weighing root, with an ability ending on top.
intro.cn: 否定前缀叠在「称量」词根上，最外层再接表能力的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- plus dispensare plus -abilis built indispensable in French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in- 加 dispensare 加 -abilis，经法语进入英语，成为 indispensable。
